w: Ten day festival.
Swamishri installed new murtis of Lord Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami, Gopalanand Swami, Hanumanji and Ganpatiji in the Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Mandir.
Morning assembly was symbolically celebrated as Pramukh Swami Maharaj's 80th Birth aniversary.
At 6.00 pm Swamishri departed from Mumbai and arrived in Vadodara at 7.22 pm. Swamishri blessed an assembly of 4,000 devotees and then left for Anand and Vidyanagar.

The day marks Dev Uthi ekadashi, Shriji Maharaj's diksha day (202nd) and appointment as head of the fellowship (201st), Pramukh Swami Maharaj's initiation into parshad (63rd years), beginning of Tulsi Vivah and end of Chaturmas.

When Swamishri arrived in the Rang Mandap for darshan of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj the sadhus chanted the 'upavit' mantras before a mock diksha scene where a cut-out murti of Swamishri was placed near the gurus' murtis.

In the evening at 6.00 pm, an Annakut of fresh vegetables was aranged before Thakorji. Swamishri performed the arti and blessed the assembly of devotees. Swamishri spoke about the sanctity the vegetables had acquired by virtue of their having been offered to God. Swamishri took hold of a brinjal, then a white raddish and finally a 'galka' in hand and spoke about their virtues.
At 11.40 a.m., Swamishri blessed a special assembly of 455 craftsmen and 25 staff members.
For the celebration of Dev Diwali an annakut had been arranged before the murtis of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj in the morning.

The festival assembly for Dev Diwali or Kartik Punam commenced immediately after Swamishri’s puja. Speeches by various sadhus followed. After Ishwarcharan Swami’s speech BAPS children and youths performed a traditional dance, “Anandno avasariyo re meheki rahyo…” Thereafter Dr. Swami and Mahant Swami addressed the assembly. This was followed by a garlanding ceremony by senior sadhus to honour and welcome Swamishri. A mantra-pushpanjali ritual was performed by 10,000 devotees to honour and offer respects to Swamishri. Finally, in his blessings, Swamishri said, “Shriji Maharaj has explained in the Vachanamrut the reason for celebrating festivals. Whosoever may remember a festival on his death bed will remember God. This will bless his soul with the attainment of the divine abode of God. So a little remembrance of God blesses a soul with redemption… Through festivals one’s morals are strengthened and many give up addictions… When Shriji Maharaj transformed the terrifying criminal called Joban Pagi peace prevailed in society. This is a great service to society…”

The daughter of Dr Bhattacharya, India's renowned heart surgeon, has married a satsangi doctor in America. Dr Bhattacharya's relative by marriage, Rambhai Panchasara, was soon to have his sixty fifth birthday. On this occasion Dr Bhattacharya wished to give him a memorable keepsake. He expressed to Tirthswarup Swami his wish to receive a letter of blessings from Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

Now the letter was being written. A sadhu told Swamishri that it would be fine even if he wrote just "May you be happy in body, mind and wealth" in his own hand. He repeated this two or three times, but Swamishri wrote, "We pray to Bhagwan Swaminarayan that you may be happy in body, mind and wealth."
Swamishri is always a servant.
Letter reading started, and it was already time to get up for the walk, but the attendant sadhu had not yet come, so Pramukh Swami Maharaj at once said, "Come, aren't there more letters?"
Dharmacharan Swami said, "It is time to go for the walk."
Swamishri said, "Until he comes, one letter or so can be read; bring it."

There were letters, but since Swamishri would be late for his walk, he said, "There are no more letters left to read." So after thinking for half a minute, Swamishri began to read the satsang magazine lying beside him. In a little while the attendant sadhus arrived.
Swamishri is ceaselessly active.

ds.t: The sacred thread for the driver
w: Before the meal, Punyanilaydas Swami, speaking of an ordinary devotee who had come to today's meetings, said, "Swami! He is a driver. His name is Jayantibhai Patel and his village is Khankuva. Today you placed your hand on his head and he was so pleased, so pleased, that he kept saying, 'I am blessed... I am blessed...'"

While this was being talked about, the attendant sadhu asked Mahant Swami Maharaj, "Do you wish to give anyone the sacred thread tied in this yagna?" He suggested the names of one or two sadhus, but Swamishri said, "No, to that driver!"

The sadhus' amazement knew no bounds. Swamishri had written this extremely rare sanctified gift into the driver's lot! But later the reason came to be known: Jayantibhai had made a wish that it would be good if he got some sanctified item of Swamishri's. And Swamishri fulfilled his wish.
